instruction:
INLAND ONLY Which is TRUE of a vessel downbound with a  following current when meeting an upbound vessel on the  Western Rivers?
Choice A: She has the right-of-way only if she is a power-driven  vessel. Choice B: She has the right-of-way only if she has a tow. Choice C: She does not have the right-of-way, since the other vessel is not crossing the river. Choice D: She must wait for a whistle signal from the upbound vessel.
response: Choice A: She has the right-of-way only if she is a power-driven  vessel.

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY What dayshape is prescribed for a vessel constrained by her draft?
Choice A: A black cone, apex upward Choice B: A black cone, apex downward Choice C: Two vertical black balls Choice D: A cylinder
response: Choice D: A cylinder

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND While underway in fog, you hear a vessel ahead sound two prolonged blasts on the whistle. You should _____.
Choice A: sound only fog signals until the other vessel is sighted Choice B: not sound any whistle signals until the other vessel is  sighted Choice C: sound two blasts and change course to the left Choice D: sound whistle signals only if you change course
response: Choice A: sound only fog signals until the other vessel is sighted

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel, which does not  normally engage in towing operations, is towing a vessel in distress. She ___________________.
Choice A: need not show the lights for a vessel engaged in towing, if it is impractical to do so Choice B: may show the lights for a vessel not under command Choice C: must show a yellow light above the sternlight Choice D: must show the lights for a vessel towing
response: Choice A: need not show the lights for a vessel engaged in towing, if it is impractical to do so

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A sailing vessel with the wind abaft the beam is navigating in fog. She should sound  ____________________.
Choice A: three short blasts Choice B: one prolonged blast Choice C: one prolonged and two short blasts Choice D: two prolonged blasts
response: Choice C: one prolonged and two short blasts

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The Navigation Rules define a "vessel not under command" as a vessel which ___________.
Choice A: from the nature of her work is unable to keep out of the way of another vessel Choice B: does not have a proper look-out Choice C: by taking action contrary to the Rules has created a  special circumstance situation Choice D: through some exceptional circumstance is unable to maneuver as required by the Rules
response: Choice D: through some exceptional circumstance is unable to maneuver as required by the Rules

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which statement is TRUE   concerning a vessel equipped with operational radar?
Choice A: She must use this equipment to obtain early warning of risk of collision. Choice B: The radar equipment is only required to be used in   restricted visibility. Choice C: The use of a radar excuses a vessel from the need of a  look-out. Choice D: The safe speed of such a vessel will likely be greater than that of vessels without radar.
response: Choice A: She must use this equipment to obtain early warning of risk of collision.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Which lights would be shown at night by a vessel which is restricted in her ability to  deviate from her course?
Choice A: Three red lights in a vertical line Choice B: Three white lights in a vertical line Choice C: Three lights in a vertical line, the highest and lowest  white and the middle red Choice D: Three lights in a vertical line, the highest and lowest red and the middle white
response: Choice D: Three lights in a vertical line, the highest and lowest red and the middle white

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND If two sailing vessels are  running free with the wind on the same side, which one must keep clear of the other?
Choice A: The one with the wind closest abeam Choice B: The one with the wind closest astern Choice C: The one to leeward Choice D: The one to windward
response: Choice D: The one to windward

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY A light used to signal passing intentions must be an ________________.
Choice A: all-round yellow light only Choice B: all-round white light only Choice C: all-round blue light only Choice D: alternating red and yellow light
response: Choice B: all-round white light only

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND What lights must sailboats show when underway at night?
Choice A: One all-round white light Choice B: A sternlight Choice C: Red and green sidelights Choice D: Red and green sidelights and a sternlight
response: Choice D: Red and green sidelights and a sternlight

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Distress signals may be _____.
Choice A: red flares Choice B: smoke signals Choice C: sound signals Choice D: Any of the above
response: Choice D: Any of the above

instruction:
INTERNATIONAL ONLY You are operating a vessel in a§narrow channel. Your vessel must stay within the channel to§be navigated safely. Another vessel is crossing your§course from starboard to port, and you are in doubt as to§his intentions. According to Rule 9, you ______.
Choice A: may sound the danger signal Choice B: must sound one prolonged and two short blasts Choice C: should sound one short blast to indicate that you are holding course and speed Choice D: are required to back down
response: Choice A: may sound the danger signal

instruction:
INLAND ONLY A barge more than 50 meters long would be  required to show how many white anchor lights when anchored in a Secretary of Transportation approved "special anchorage area"?
Choice A: 1 Choice B: 2 Choice C: 3 Choice D: 4
response: Choice B: 2

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Dayshapes must be displayed _____.
Choice A: between sunset and sunrise Choice B: only between 8 AM and 4 PM Choice C: during daylight hours in any visibility Choice D: during daylight hours in unrestricted visibility only
response: Choice C: during daylight hours in any visibility

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A traffic separation zone is that part of a traffic separation scheme which ________.
Choice A: is between the scheme and the nearest land Choice B: contains all the traffic moving in one direction Choice C: is designated as an anchorage area Choice D: separates traffic proceeding in one direction from traffic proceeding in the opposite direction
response: Choice D: separates traffic proceeding in one direction from traffic proceeding in the opposite direction

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Navigation lights must be  displayed in all weathers from sunset to sunrise. They also _________________.
Choice A: must be displayed when day signals are being used Choice B: must be displayed when moored to a pier Choice C: may be extinguished at night on open waters when no other vessels are in the area Choice D: may be displayed during daylight
response: Choice D: may be displayed during daylight

instruction:
INLAND ONLY Which type of vessel is NOT mentioned in the Inland Navigation Rules?
Choice A: An inconspicuous, partly submerged vessel Choice B: A seaplane Choice C: An air-cushion vessel Choice D: A vessel constrained by her draft
response: Choice D: A vessel constrained by her draft

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A power-driven vessel underway shall keep out of the way of a _________________.
Choice A: vessel not under command Choice B: vessel engaged in fishing Choice C: sailing vessel Choice D: All of the above
response: Choice D: All of the above

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND Three short blasts of the  whistle means _______________.
Choice A: "danger" Choice B: "I am in distress" Choice C: "my vessel is towing" Choice D: "I am operating astern propulsion"
response: Choice D: "I am operating astern propulsion"

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A power-driven vessel, when  towing astern, shall show _____.
Choice A: two towing lights in a vertical line Choice B: a towing light in a vertical line above the sternlight Choice C: two towing lights in addition to the sternlight Choice D: a small white light in lieu of the sternlight
response: Choice B: a towing light in a vertical line above the sternlight

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel engaged in fishing  underway sounds the same fog signal as a _________________.
Choice A: power-driven vessel stopped and making no way through the water Choice B: vessel being towed Choice C: vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver at anchor Choice D: sailing vessel at anchor
response: Choice C: vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver at anchor

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND You see another vessel   approaching, and its compass bearing does not significantly change. This would indicate that _____.
Choice A: you are the stand-on vessel Choice B: risk of collision exists Choice C: a special circumstances situation exists Choice D: the other vessel is dead in the water
response: Choice B: risk of collision exists

instruction:
INLAND ONLY What is the whistle signal used to indicate a power-driven vessel leaving a dock?
Choice A: One short blast Choice B: Three short blasts Choice C: One prolonged blast Choice D: Three prolonged blasts
response: Choice C: One prolonged blast

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A power-driven vessel making way through the water sounds which fog signal?
Choice A: Two short blasts every one minute Choice B: One short blast every one minute Choice C: Two prolonged blasts every two minutes Choice D: One prolonged blast every two minutes
response: Choice D: One prolonged blast every two minutes

instruction:
INLAND ONLY Which statement is TRUE concerning a passing agreement made by radiotelephone?
Choice A: Such an agreement is prohibited by the Rules. Choice B: A vessel which has made such an agreement must also sound whistle signals. Choice C: Whistle signals must still be exchanged when passing within half a mile of each other. Choice D: If agreement is reached by radiotelephone, whistle signals are optional.
response: Choice D: If agreement is reached by radiotelephone, whistle signals are optional.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A power-driven vessel towing astern shall show _____.
Choice A: two towing lights in a vertical line Choice B: a towing light in a vertical line above the sternlight Choice C: two towing lights in addition to the sternlight Choice D: a small white light in lieu of the sternlight
response: Choice B: a towing light in a vertical line above the sternlight

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND The whistle signal for a vessel operating astern propulsion is _________________.
Choice A: one long blast Choice B: one prolonged blast Choice C: three short blasts Choice D: four or more short blasts
response: Choice C: three short blasts

instruction:
INLAND ONLY While underway and in sight of another vessel§a mile ahead you put your engines on astern propulsion. §Which statement concerning whistle signals is TRUE?
Choice A: You must sound three short blasts on the whistle. Choice B: You must sound one blast if backing to starboard. Choice C: You must sound whistle signals only if the vessels are meeting. Choice D: You need not sound any whistle signals.
response: Choice D: You need not sound any whistle signals.

instruction:
BOTH INTERNATIONAL & INLAND A vessel nearing a bend where other vessels may be obscured shall sound _______________.
Choice A: one short blast Choice B: one long blast Choice C: two short blasts Choice D: one prolonged blast
response: Choice D: one prolonged blast
